implementation_notes: TypeScript has no built-in DbC syntax. The `@frenchexdev/ddd-dbc` package provides decorator-based `@Pre`, `@Post` and `@Invariant` contracts; use its documented exports, or define a native assertion function with an `asserts` return type when a dependency is not warranted. Runtime decorators must evaluate side-effect-free predicates, while schema parsing belongs at trust boundaries and ordinary guards/typed errors handle expected input failures.
pitfalls: Wrong move: import from `@frenchexdev/dbc` or assume `@AggregateRoot` is exported by the contract package -> Failure: the module or decorator is unresolved at build time -> Instead: use the documented `@frenchexdev/ddd-dbc` exports and import aggregate decorators separately.
String predicates lose ordinary TypeScript refactoring and type-checking support compared with in-code functions; keep expressions small and cover them with runtime tests.
Decorators only protect decorated entry points; an exposed field or undecorated mutator can bypass the invariant -> Instead: encapsulate state and route every mutation through the decorated API.
